bullets.title: S&P 500 logs worst week since April 2025 — 7-day losing streak, NDX -10%
bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell ~8.6% for the week (worst since April 2025) with seven consecutive daily declines, the longest streak since February 2020. Nasdaq dropped 10% and is now negative YTD after hitting ATH on October 6. Breadth was extremely weak — decliners outnumbered gainers 15:1 on Friday, and 68% of global equity market indices were oversold per BofA. Goldman estimated $57B in CTA selling over the past month.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness is the macro driver: Waller signals 50bp December hike, market forced to price out the 'Fed put'
bullets.body: Governor Waller suggested a 50bp December hike may be necessary, with other Fed officials (Musalem, Logan, Goolsbee) also signaling resolve to reach 2% PCE even if growth slows. Markets are now pricing 62bps of hikes over the next 10 months. Morgan Stanley's base case is 25bp in December and March, then hold through 2027. Multiple strategists noted the Fed is shifting from risk-management to inflation-credibility mode — meaning the traditional equity 'circuit breaker' may not trigger. 2-year yields fell 24bp on the week but remain elevated as markets began tentatively pricing a pivot before the December 9 meeting.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning at multi-year lows — extreme net selling, semis most sold, defensive rotation at dot-com bust levels
bullets.body: Global HF net selling over 20 days was approximately -2 sigma; North America exceeded -2 sigma. Net leverage fell from 12-month highs to the 26th percentile over five years, with Equity L/S at the 21st percentile. US semis were the most net-sold group for two months straight. The rotation out of Tech into Defensives is at levels not seen since the dot-com bust — Utilities, Telecom, Pharma & Biotech, and Real Estate all saw defensive inflows. Systematic net leverage collapsed from the 80th to the 25th 5-year percentile since early October.

bullets.title: AI trade repricing: export controls, capital constraints, ROI doubts pile on top of NVDA leadership vacuum
bullets.body: The AI selloff accelerated on multiple fronts: (1) new BIS export rules require licenses for chip sales to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Brazil and block Chinese remote access to US data center compute; (2) NVDA's server partners halted SE Asia shipments; (3) an SEC civil probe into NVDA accounting practices was opened; (4) NVDA interim CEO signaled more selective neocloud financing; and (5) Trump announced tax penalties for US companies building data centers abroad. NVDA extended its decline to -47% from all-time highs despite a beat-and-raise quarter. The AI Infrastructure index (MSXXAI) fell -15% week-over-week.

bullets.title: US-China tech war escalates: TSMC/Samsung halt China shipments, BIS IFR closes compute loopholes
bullets.body: The Commerce Department issued an interim final rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips, rescinding Biden's AI Diffusion Rule and replacing it with stricter controls. TSMC and Samsung suspended advanced chip shipments (16nm and below) to Chinese customers pending US license reviews. BABA warned new US rules will affect 2027 products and pivoted to in-house T-Head chips. The MATCH Act, which would restrict ASML tool exports to China, is odds-on for NDAA inclusion. China retaliation risk is rising, centered on rare earths and critical minerals.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals confirm risk-off: gold -9.5%, copper -9.9%, Bitcoin -15%, oil -5.8%
bullets.body: Gold had its worst week since March, silver fell 16.4% (worst since January), copper fell 9.9% for a sixth straight weekly decline (the -4.3 SD move signals AI/data center demand concerns and China worries). Bitcoin futures were down 15.5% for a seventh consecutive weekly decline near June two-year lows. WTI crude fell 5.8% as improved supply/demand dynamics offset Iran-US tensions. Dollar strength, crypto/commodity weakness, and rising real yields signal the real-rate shock is still propagating.

bullets.title: Data center permitting crackdown: 30+ moratoriums passed, Texas freeze, Georgia opposition, Loudoun County pause
bullets.body: Thirty of thirty-one data-center moratoriums passed during election week. Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa announced a permit moratorium and plans to repeal sales tax exemptions, potentially putting 30% of 2028 GW pipeline at risk per SemiAnalysis. Arizona AG sought to delay SpaceX's $50B campus hearing. North Carolina's Governor called for phasing out public subsidies. Loudoun County, VA adopted a 12-month pause. Texas TCEQ did resume air permit issuance mid-week but the ERCOT comprehensive audit on December 10 remains a key gating event.

bullets.title: Treasuries rallied on safe-haven demand despite hawkish Fed; 10Y fell to ~4.91% by Friday
bullets.body: Treasuries rallied sharply Friday as equities fell — 10-year yields dropped 14bp to ~4.91% and 2-year yields fell 16.6bp to 4.61%. The 20-year auction stopped on the screws with solid foreign participation. Despite the rally, 30-year yields remain near highs. JPMorgan forecasts 2027 Treasury demand of approximately $1.38T but notes the bill-heavy funding mix reduces duration pressure.

bullets.title: SPX technical damage severe: broke 7,200 support, below 200-day MA; targets 7,000 then 6,500
bullets.body: The S&P 500 broke below 7,200 support and all major indices (SPX, NDX, Russell) closed below their 200-day moving averages for the week — a combination that has occurred only six times since 2008. The NDX broke 24,000; next stops 22,000 then 20,000. The SOX is approaching multi-year valuation lows. Five failing clearing events over six weeks indicate bear market conditions. Historically, periods of large HF net selling coinciding with sell-offs are followed by rebounds within a month, but that pattern has not yet confirmed this cycle.

bullets.title: Tactical bounce case: $50B pension buying, options skew at extreme, $3.6T OPEX on Nov 20
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS estimated ~$50B in pension/asset allocator buying at current price levels (SPX -3%). SPX Put vs Call Vol spread (25-delta, 3M/1Y) hit 9.66 — historically in the top <10% since 2013, with +3.6% average return over the next two months (1.73x Sharpe). The November 20 options expiration included ~$3.6T notional ($900B delta, 75% puts), creating significant mechanical pressure. Street short gamma likely amplifies moves in both directions. Despite elevated VIX (28-30), retail was a net buyer of ~$29B in US equities through the drawdown.

bullets.title: Consumer remains resilient: October retail sales beat, holiday spending off to a strong start
bullets.body: October control-group retail sales rose +0.6% m/m, beating consensus of +0.3%, and prior months were revised up 70bp. BofA data shows holiday spending off to a strong start with spending growth converging across income groups. Real PCE is tracking ~2.5% annualized in Q4 vs. Bloomberg consensus of 2%. However, University of Michigan consumer sentiment printed 51.5, slightly below consensus, while NAHB homebuilder sentiment hit a 14-year low and pending home sales fell 4.7% m/m to a record low — the housing market remains severely constrained by rates.

bullets.title: AI users outperforming on margins and productivity even as infrastructure stocks collapse
bullets.body: S&P 1500 companies with clear AI usage show accelerating sales-per-employee growth and rising forward net margin expectations — contrasting with declining expectations for non-AI users. About 50% of S&P 1500 companies now use AI, up from 20% in 2024. 22V estimates narrowly defined AI explains 22% of aggregate demand growth YTD; broadly defined AI explains 42%. This divergence between AI infrastructure (crashing) and AI adopters (margin expansion) is the key positioning theme heading into 2027.

bullets.title: Russia-Ukraine escalation: Kerch Bridge destroyed, Russian missile retaliation, EU considering €45B in new aid
bullets.body: Ukraine destroyed the Kerch Bridge, a major strategic and logistical blow to Russian operations in Crimea. Russian retaliation is underway with missiles falling in Ukraine and neighboring Poland. Trump dismissed strikes in Poland as 'a couple of little missiles, by mistake.' The EU is discussing an additional €45B in Ukraine aid at November 26-27 meetings. The Xi-Trump-Putin APEC declaration in Shenzhen made no reference to Ukraine and committed the three powers to increase refined petroleum production. Cyber security incidents from the conflict constitute a broad supply shock that is directionally inflationary.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley raises S&P 500 12-month target to 8,700; sees correction as mid-cycle reset, not end of bull market
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson raised the S&P 500 price target to 8,700 (19x forward EPS of $458) based on 2026 EPS of $369 (+34%), 2027 $420 (+14%), and 2028 $458 (+9%). The bull case rests on healthy earnings growth, lower oil, stabilizing rate volatility, and broadening AI adoption. Goldman Sachs also targets 8,700 by year-end 2027 with EPS growth slowing to 18% in 2027 from ~30% in 2026. At current levels, the S&P 500 implies roughly 20%+ upside to these year-end targets.

bullets.title: EM/global risk: Korea/Taiwan tech selloff deepens, Nikkei down 22% from AI bubble peak, EM flows still positive
bullets.body: Taiwan's equity index crashed -6.2% this week; the Nikkei dropped -5.1%, taking a -22% loss from the AI bubble peak in June. Korea's semiconductor export business confidence is clearly declining, and semiconductor sales growth is expected to slow from 108% YoY in 2026 to just 29% in 2027. Despite this, EM equity funds posted their seventh consecutive week of inflows at +$2.4B, with India accelerating to +$4.2B and Taiwan outflows moderating. Jefferies is downgrading Korea and Taiwan on AI capex deceleration risk while favoring India and quality stocks.

bullets.title: JPMorgan 2027 US economic outlook: AI capex moderates, consumer slows, three Fed hikes to 4.5-4.75%
bullets.body: JPM's 2027 US economic outlook calls for AI-related capex growth to moderate from 10% (2026) to 8% (2027), real consumer spending to slow from 2.6% to 1.7%, and three Fed hikes in December, January, and March bringing the funds rate to 4.5-4.75%. Core PCE is expected to remain in the mid-to-high 2% range. AI-related spending could boost productivity by ~0.5pp per year. The key risk is that stronger-than-expected consumer spending forces additional tightening.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler funding gap: $450B AI supply forecast for 2027, $595B aggregate FCF shortfall 2027-28
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts $450B in AI-related debt and equity supply in 2027 — $225B from parent-level hyperscaler issuance and $225B from GPU/data center project financing. Hyperscalers are forecast to be FCF-negative in aggregate through 2028, with a ~$595B funding gap across 2027-2028. JPM downgrades Alphabet to Neutral from Overweight due to tighter valuations and Search durability concerns; retains Overweight on Amazon and Oracle. NVDA's tightening of neocloud financing raises capital costs for smaller operators.

bullets.title: Global defensive rotation unprecedented since dot-com bust; staples at 15% premium to S&P 500
bullets.body: Defensive stocks outpaced cyclicals by up to 15 percentage points in a month across US and Europe — a rotation size typically seen only in major stress episodes (2008, 2020, 2022). XLP traded to its widest premium to the S&P 500 since December 2022. The Morgan Stanley Cross-Asset Risk Monitor composite reads -0.68, with 19 of 34 indicators flashing, but stress is concentrated in equities (volatility, correlation, beta) rather than credit or rates, which distinguishes this from the 2022 bear market so far.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike in acquisition talks with Zscaler; ZS +18% after-hours
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler. ZS shares surged 18% in after-hours trading on the news. No terms were disclosed.
